notes: Caves is the hardest arena to learn and the one where that knowledge pays most. It is dark, irregular and tightly packed -- the smallest pad count in the game carrying the joint-most spawn points, which is why contacts happen constantly and orientation is difficult.
See mp/_general.json for the cross-arena layer.

nuance.claim: The layout is genuinely hard to internalise, so a player who knows it holds a bigger edge here than on any other arena; the map rewards study rather than reflexes.
Unlit stretches genuinely conceal a player, which makes this the only arena where standing still is sometimes correct.
Concealment stops working once opponents learn where you sit, so the shadows are used to break contact and reposition rather than as a permanent position.
Character choice matters more here than anywhere else: a dark-clothed character in a dark arena is meaningfully harder to see, which compounds with the map's own concealment.
The arena packs the joint-most spawn points into the least space, so respawns happen close to the action and re-entry into a fight is fast for everyone.
nuance.because: Caves carries eight Spawn records across only thirty-five pads, the highest spawn density of any arena.

nuance.claim: Eight spawn points cannot be covered, so holding a reappearance point is wasted effort; controlling a junction is the better use of position.
nuance.because: Caves carries eight Spawn records, joint most in the game.

nuance.claim: Two armours in a map this small means both are close to everything, so contesting them is cheap and neglecting them is costly.
nuance.because: Caves carries two Armour records across thirty-five pads, the tightest armour spacing of any arena.

nuance.claim: The rock walls are uneven rather than flat, so sightlines open and close with small movements and an opponent can be lost without deliberately breaking contact.
Because vision is unreliable, hearing is the primary way opponents are located here and moving quietly is worth more than moving fast.
The passages meet at a small number of junctions, and holding one covers several routes at once, which is the closest thing this arena has to a power position.
Junctions are the highest-traffic points on the map and are approached in darkness, which makes mines there unusually hard to spot in time.
The passages are tight and the walls uneven, so explosives clip geometry and detonate short far more often than on the built arenas.
There are almost no long clear sightlines and the lighting defeats what few exist, so precision weapons are among the weakest choices here.
One-hit kills plus real concealment make ambush overwhelming, so this mode on this map is decided almost entirely by who is seen first.
A defenceless carrier does unusually well, because the darkness and irregular passages break pursuit repeatedly even without any weapon to threaten pursuers.
A marked holder benefits from the concealment more than the hunters benefit from the marker, which makes this the friendliest arena to hold the gun on.
